events.title: An evening at Anna's
events.summary: In July 1805, Anna Pavlovna greets Prince Vasili at her Petersburg reception; politics enters through the drawing room.

events.title: A marriage proposed in conversation
events.summary: Anna suggests Mary Bolkonskaya as a match for Anatole. Vasili immediately asks about her wealth.

events.title: Pierre enters society
events.summary: The narrator introduces Pierre as Count Bezukhov's illegitimate son, newly returned from education abroad.

events.title: Andrew chooses military service
events.summary: Andrew says Kutuzov has taken him as an aide-de-camp. His wife will go to the country.

events.title: The Rostov children burst in
events.summary: A thirteen-year-old girl interrupts the formal reception: Natasha's energy changes the scene.

events.title: A death becomes a social narrative
events.summary: After Count Bezukhov's death, Anna Mikhaylovna recounts an edifying version to the Rostovs and her acquaintances.

events.title: The household at Bald Hills
events.summary: The narrative enters the old Prince Bolkonsky's disciplined country household, where Mary lives with her father.

events.title: The Austrian defeat reaches headquarters
events.summary: The report of Mack's surrender at Ulm is confirmed; the Russian troops must prepare to meet the enemy.

events.title: Tushin's retreat
events.summary: As the Schongraben fighting subsides, orders, reproaches, wounded men, and the withdrawing guns crowd together.

events.title: Pierre becomes the wealthy heir
events.summary: Pierre is now Count Bezukhov; paperwork, visitors, and other people's expectations consume his newly inherited life.

events.title: Pierre marries Helene
events.summary: The chapter closes by announcing their marriage six weeks later and their establishment in Petersburg.

events.title: Mary refuses the proposed marriage
events.summary: In front of Vasili and her father, Mary declares that she does not wish to marry.

events.title: The council before Austerlitz
events.summary: Weyrother presents his battle plans to the assembled commanders; Kutuzov presides reluctantly.

events.title: The sky over Austerlitz
events.summary: Falling wounded, Andrew sees the immense sky and experiences the collapse of his former scale of values.

events.title: Napoleon passes the wounded Andrew
events.summary: Napoleon surveys the battlefield and stops beside Andrew, who lies with the fallen flagstaff.

events.title: Pierre fires at Dolokhov
events.summary: In their duel, Pierre fires almost mechanically; Dolokhov appears through the smoke holding his side.

events.title: Lise dies in childbirth
events.summary: Andrew hears the infant's cry, then enters his wife's room and finds her dead.

events.title: Sonya refuses Dolokhov
events.summary: Natasha tells Nicholas that Dolokhov proposed and Sonya refused, saying that she loved another.

events.title: Nicholas's gambling debt
events.summary: Nicholas's losses to Dolokhov reach forty-three thousand rubles, before the final addition of twenty-one.

events.title: An invitation to Freemasonry
events.summary: Pierre is offered sponsorship into the Brotherhood of Freemasons as he seeks moral renewal.

events.title: The reforms Pierre cannot see
events.summary: The narrator distinguishes Pierre's optimistic impression of his estates from the harsher conditions concealed from him.

events.title: Pierre visits Andrew
events.summary: Returning from his southern estates, Pierre visits the friend he has not seen for two years.

events.title: The emperors at Tilsit
events.summary: The French and Russian emperors arrive at Tilsit, while Boris secures a place in the attending suite.

events.title: The transformed oak
events.summary: On his return journey Andrew recognizes the oak in leaf and feels an unexpected renewal of life.

events.title: Natasha and Andrew dance
events.summary: At Pierre's prompting, Andrew invites Natasha to waltz at her first great ball.

events.title: A proposal under a year's delay
events.summary: Andrew asks the countess for Natasha's hand after agreeing to his father's demand that the wedding be postponed for a year.

events.title: Natasha's Russian dance
events.summary: At Uncle's home, Natasha's dance astonishes Anisya Fyodorovna with its instinctive precision.

events.title: Nicholas and Sonya in disguise
events.summary: During the Christmas festivities, Nicholas kisses Sonya under the moonlight, her disguise still smelling of burnt cork.

events.title: Boris and Julie become engaged
events.summary: Their engagement is followed by plans for a splendid house and a brilliant wedding.

events.title: Anatole's concealed marriage
events.summary: The narrator reveals that Anatole married in Poland two years earlier, a fact known only to his closest friends.

events.title: Sonya finds the letter
events.summary: Sonya discovers and reads Anatole's letter beside the sleeping Natasha.

events.title: The planned elopement
events.summary: Dolokhov has arranged the preparations for Anatole to carry Natasha away.

events.title: Pierre offers Natasha tenderness
events.summary: Pierre tells Natasha that if he were free and the best man imaginable, he would ask for her hand.

events.title: Europe moves east
events.summary: The narrator opens the 1812 campaign by contrasting immense collective movement with explanations resting on individual motives.

events.title: Alexander sends Balashev
events.summary: Alexander sends a letter to Napoleon and repeats his refusal to make peace while an armed enemy remains on Russian soil.

events.title: Mary escapes Bogucharovo
events.summary: After the confrontation with the peasants, Nicholas accompanies Mary's carriage to the Russian lines.

events.title: Pierre seeks the battlefield
events.summary: On the eve of Borodino, Pierre tells Andrew that he has come to see the battle.

events.title: Andrew wounded at Borodino
events.summary: An explosion wounds Andrew in the abdomen, and he is carried toward the dressing station.

events.title: Andrew recognizes Anatole
events.summary: At the dressing station, Andrew recognizes Anatole after an amputation; memories of Natasha return with a new tenderness.

events.title: The order to abandon Moscow
events.summary: At the council at Fili, Kutuzov takes responsibility and orders a retreat.

events.title: Carts for the wounded
events.summary: Natasha protests against preserving the family's possessions instead of using the carts for wounded soldiers.

events.title: Natasha learns Andrew is nearby
events.summary: Sonya tells Natasha that the wounded Andrew is traveling with their party; the countess had wanted this concealed.

events.title: Natasha and Andrew reconciled
events.summary: Natasha asks forgiveness; Andrew tells her that he loves her more and better than before.

events.title: Pierre meets Platon Karataev
events.summary: In captivity, Karataev introduces himself and speaks to Pierre in the rhythms of consolation and proverbial wisdom.

events.title: Andrew's death
events.summary: Mary and Natasha attend Andrew's final moments; Natasha closes his eyes.

events.title: Causes beyond a single cause
events.summary: The narrator argues that human understanding seizes on partial causes because it cannot grasp events in their full complexity.

events.title: Petya dies; Pierre is rescued
events.summary: Petya is killed in the raid. The chapter then identifies Pierre among the Russian prisoners rescued by Denisov and Dolokhov.

events.title: The shot behind the prisoners
events.summary: Pierre hears a shot from where Karataev had been sitting; the narrative conveys his killing indirectly through sound, soldiers, and avoidance.

events.title: Natasha and Pierre marry
events.summary: The epilogue identifies their 1813 wedding as the last happy event in the old Rostovs' family before the count's death that year.

events.title: Nicholas and Mary establish a household
events.summary: Nicholas marries Mary in the winter of 1813 and moves to Bald Hills with her, his mother, and Sonya.

events.title: Politics divides the family circle
events.summary: Pierre defends an association for public welfare; Nicholas regards a secret society as harmful.

events.title: Freedom and necessity
events.summary: The final chapter uses the Copernican transformation as an analogy for changing how historical necessity is understood.

knowledge.claim: Anna proposes Mary as a possible wife for Anatole.
knowledge.note: A proposal exchanged between Anna and Vasili; no consent or knowledge by the prospective couple is established here.

knowledge.claim: Anatole costs Vasili forty thousand rubles a year.
knowledge.note: Vasili's own financial claim, not an independently audited amount.

knowledge.claim: Kutuzov has taken Andrew as an aide-de-camp.
knowledge.note: Andrew answers Anna directly at the reception.

knowledge.claim: Vasili promises to arrange Boris's transfer to the Guards.
knowledge.note: A promise of patronage; this utterance alone does not establish completed appointment.

knowledge.claim: Lise has been told about Anna's proposed match for Anatole.
knowledge.note: The narrator reports a conversation that has already occurred; the reader receives it after the fact.

knowledge.claim: Nicholas kisses Sonya while Natasha watches from hiding.
knowledge.note: The immediately preceding paragraph supplies the kiss; Natasha's observation is explicit. This does not prove the couple never noticed her.

knowledge.claim: Anna Mikhaylovna circulates an edifying account of Count Bezukhov's death.
knowledge.note: The narration marks a gap between Pierre's incomprehension and the confident public account; the recipient field represents the Rostov household.

knowledge.claim: Andrew's experience of the sky radically diminishes his former ambitions.
knowledge.note: Interior discourse is available to the reader. No act of telling another character is recorded in this passage.

knowledge.claim: Sonya refused Dolokhov's proposal and said she loved another.
knowledge.note: Nicholas receives the news through Natasha before speaking with Sonya.

knowledge.claim: Pierre does not know the harsh conditions hidden behind his estate reforms.
knowledge.note: Reader advantage: the narrator explicitly lists what Pierre does not know. Holder here is the character whose knowledge is being described, not the possessor of the hidden facts.

knowledge.claim: Andrew agrees to his father's requested one-year postponement.
knowledge.note: The demand appears in the preceding paragraph; Andrew's decision to conform follows. Natasha has not yet been informed at this point in the chapter.

knowledge.claim: Natasha cannot explain Andrew's absence because she does not know he has gone to his father.
knowledge.note: An explicit local knowledge gap, not an inference from missing dialogue.

knowledge.claim: Anatole is already married; only his closest friends know.
knowledge.note: The reader receives the secret from the narrator. The passage does not name every person in the circle of informed friends.

knowledge.claim: Sonya learns the contents of Anatole's letter to Natasha.
knowledge.note: Sonya reads the open letter while Natasha sleeps; the communication was not addressed to Sonya.

knowledge.claim: Dolokhov warns Anatole that his existing marriage will be discovered.
knowledge.note: This establishes Dolokhov's knowledge of the prior marriage as well as his warning about legal consequences.

knowledge.claim: Pierre already knows Anatole is secretly married when he learns of the attempted elopement.
knowledge.note: The narrator explicitly says 'as Pierre knew'; the date and source of his earlier knowledge are not supplied.

knowledge.claim: Andrew tells Pierre that he cannot forgive Natasha.
knowledge.note: A statement of Andrew's present feeling, not a permanent psychological fact.

knowledge.claim: Pierre tells Natasha he would seek her hand if he were free and worthy.
knowledge.note: Conditional language matters: this is not a marriage proposal or engagement.

knowledge.claim: Alexander tells Balashev he will not make peace while armed enemies remain on Russian soil.
knowledge.note: An instruction conveyed with a diplomatic letter to Napoleon.

knowledge.claim: Mary is not safely in Moscow as Andrew supposes.
knowledge.note: The opening sentence explicitly contrasts Andrew's belief with Mary's actual situation. Holder identifies the mistaken believer.

knowledge.claim: Andrew recognizes the wounded man at the dressing station as Anatole.
knowledge.note: Recognition is narrated from Andrew's experience; it is not information deliberately sent by Anatole.

knowledge.claim: Sonya tells Natasha that wounded Andrew is traveling with their party.
knowledge.note: The countess is angered by the disclosure. The narrator reports it retrospectively from that morning.

knowledge.claim: Andrew tells Natasha that he loves her more and better than before.
knowledge.note: Compare his refusal to forgive in Book VIII, chapter XXI; the utterances belong to different moments.

knowledge.claim: Karataev tells Pierre how military service spared his brother's family.
knowledge.note: A personal recollection told by Karataev, with its meaning of misfortune becoming blessing.

knowledge.claim: Pierre hears a shot from where Karataev was sitting but turns to calculation instead.
knowledge.note: The shot is heard, not visually witnessed. The killing is conveyed indirectly; avoid turning this into an explicit eyewitness account.

relations.label: husband and wife at this point

methodology: Editorial selections, not an exhaustive scene inventory. Each reference is a global chapter ID (1–365) and zero-based paragraph index in text.json. Knowledge records distinguish explicit narration, interior discourse, reports, letters, and witnessed experience. An absent record never establishes ignorance. The holder identifies the focal character for narrated knowledge gaps. Relationships are historical observations at the cited chapter, not a claim of permanent current status. Event years are broad story-time labels; philosophic chapters inherit their surrounding narrative period rather than a literal event date. Some events combine facts from adjacent paragraphs within the cited chapter.
